about: Rich nearby clusters whose members' velocities are dominated by motion inside the cluster (object framework sections 18.4.6 and 18.18 item 3). A galaxy that would otherwise get a Hubble-flow distance is a member when it lies within `radius_deg` of the cluster centre on the sky and its heliocentric velocity is within 3 sigma of the CF4 group's heliocentric velocity (Colless & Dunn 1996 selected Coma members by 3-sigma clipping). A member is placed at the CF4 group distance, method group-member (derived), with the interval widened in quadrature by the cluster radius along the line of sight. Every number carries `src` and `where`, read in the paper text on 2026-11-19. Centaurus (Abell 3526) is left out: no radius was found in a paper (Stein et al. 1997 give none).
